text: Understanding databases is essential for anyone working with data. There are two main types: SQL and NoSQL. SQL databases store information in tables, which are organised rows and columns, much like a spreadsheet. To get data from these tables, you write queries—special commands that ask specific questions. Good data modeling helps you plan how tables connect before you build anything. Indexes are another useful tool: they work like a book's index, helping the database find information quickly without scanning every row. NoSQL databases, on the other hand, are more flexible and suit different needs. Choosing the right type depends on your project.
